findings.reason: decimal.js:2153 now only validates rm and never sets rm = Ctor.rounding. The undefined rm reaches divide and then finalise (decimal.js:3011-3017), where `undefined < 4` is false and `rm == 4/6/7/8` are all false, so an exact 5 never rounds up. With the default ROUND_HALF_UP, new Decimal(2.5).toNearest(1) gives 2. This contradicts the doc comment at decimal.js:2120-2121 and every sibling method (e.g. :1953, :2372).
findings.claim: When a multiple y is given and rm is left out, toNearest no longer falls back to Decimal.rounding. rm stays undefined, so ties round half-down and the configured rounding mode is ignored.
findings.evidence: The diff swaps `if (rm === void 0) { rm = Ctor.rounding; } else { checkInt32(rm, 0, 8); }` for `if (rm !== void 0) checkInt32(rm, 0, 8);`, so `rm` stays undefined. It goes on to `divide(x, y, 0, rm, 1)` and then `finalise(q, ..., rm, more)`. In finalise, `roundUp = rm < 4 ? ... : rd > 5 || rd == 5 && (rm == 4 || isTruncated || rm == 6 && ... || rm == (x.s < 0 ? 8 : 7))`: with rm undefined, a plain 5 never rounds up. The rounding mode is also ignored for non-ties, e.g. Decimal.rounding = ROUND_UP no longer applies. This contradicts the method's own doc comment at decimal.js:2120-2121 ('the rounding mode `rm`, or `Decimal.rounding` if `rm` is omitted') and doc/API.html:2224-2226. None of the story's tests needed this change.

findings.reason: Every call that passes y without rm (toNearest.js:75-88) uses 123.456, which is never an exact tie. The calls that set Decimal.rounding (lines 153-157) pass void 0 for y, so they take the y == null branch, which still sets rm = Ctor.rounding at decimal.js:2150.
findings.claim: No locked test calls toNearest with an explicit y, rm omitted and an exact tie, so the C1 regression passes the suite.
findings.evidence: Every call that passes `y` without `rm` (lines 75-88, e.g. `t('123', 123.456, 1)`, `t('123.4', 123.456, '-0.2')`) has a rounding digit other than an exact 5. Every test that sets Decimal.rounding (lines 153-157) passes `void 0` for `y`, so it takes the `y == null` branch, which still sets `rm = Ctor.rounding`.

findings.reason: The divergence is real: decimal.js:2168 checks `rm === 1 || rm === 3`, while decimal.mjs:2166 has `rm < 4`. But the locked tests require directed rounding for modes 0 and 2 (toNearest.js:115, 117, 159), which the mjs mapping would fail. Without the story I can't tell whether the ESM build was meant to change, so I'm lowering severity to low.
findings.claim: decimal.js now maps only modes 1 and 3 to half modes, while the untouched decimal.mjs maps all modes below 4, so CommonJS and ESM builds give different results for modes 0 and 2. The doc comment at :2123-2124 matches neither build.
findings.evidence: decimal.js:2168 has `if (rm === 1 || rm === 3) rm = [4, 5, 7, 8][rm];`, so the entries 4 and 7 can never be used. decimal.mjs:2166, which the diff leaves alone, has `if (rm < 4) rm = [4, 5, 7, 8][rm];`. So new Decimal('3847561.00000749').toNearest(10, 0) gives '3847570' from decimal.js (as the test at toNearest.js:159 expects) but '3847560' from decimal.mjs. decimal.min.js was not rebuilt either. The doc comment at decimal.js:2123-2124 ('rounding mode 4 (ROUND_HALF_UP) is the same as rounding mode 0 (ROUND_UP), and so on') describes neither behaviour.

findings.reason: The locked tests expect this directed behaviour. toNearest.js:115 expects '83105511540' for 83105511539.4 with mode 0, line 117 expects the same with mode 2, and line 159 expects '3847570' for 3847561.00000749 to 10 with mode 0. Mapping 0 and 2 to half modes would fail those acceptance tests, so this is the specified behaviour, not a defect.
findings.claim: Leaving modes 0 and 2 unmapped lets toNearest return a multiple farther away than the nearest one.
findings.evidence: The new condition converts only rm === 1 or rm === 3, leaving modes 0 and 2 as directed rounding in divide/finalise. Executing new Decimal(1.1).toNearest(1, 0) or toNearest(1, 2) returns '2', although the nearest multiple is '1'. The existing decimal.mjs implementation converts all modes below 4 using the same mapping and returns '1' for both examples.
